newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal's Deuba on way to palace with resignation.
newsitem.headline: Nepal's Deuba on way to palace with resignation.

text.p: Nepali Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba left for King Birendra's palace to tender his resignation on Thursday after his government was defeated in a confidence vote in parliament, witnesses said.

"I am going to the palace with my resignation," Deuba told Reuters after his 17-month-old centre-right coalition failed to win the required 103 votes in a confidence motion he moved in the 205-seat lower house of parliament.

Deuba's government received 101 votes against a required minimum of 103 during voting on the motion, which he had moved to try to demonstrate the coalition's majority. A total of 92 deputies voted against the motion.
Lawmakers said two of Deuba's Nepali Congress party lawmakers were not present for the voting. There was no official confirmation of their absence.
The Nepali Congress party, which has 87 seats, lost its majority last December following a split in the ranks of one of its two partners, the Rashtriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), which had 19 seats.
The opposition communist United Marxist-Leninist (UML) party and its allies control 94 votes.
